newsitem.title: DUBAI: China tops Oman crude customer list.
newsitem.headline: China tops Oman crude customer list.

text.p: China was the single largest customer of Omani crude in May, buying the equivalent of 241,354 barrels per day (bpd) out of total exports of 853,709 bpd, according to figures released by Oman's Ministry of Development.
Thailand was the Gulf sultanate's second largest lifter at 216,709 bpd followed by Japan at 201,387 bpd.
Oman's total crude exports in May reached 26,465,000 barrels, up from 24,988,000 barrels in April.
Oman oil output averaged 887,548 bpd in May, compared to an average rate of 885,010 for 1996, the ministry said.

The country's single refinery processed 2,256,600 barrels of crude in May, producing 2,150,500 barrels of refined products. The plant processed 763,000 barrels in April as the refinery came out of maintenance work which stopped March operations.

Output of super-gasoline (97-octane) was 231,400 barrels, regular-gasoline (90-octane) 96,900 barrels, jet A-1 84,200, gas oil 5,166,000 barrels, long residue 1,182,200 barrels and butane 174 39,200 barrels.
Net oil revenue in May was 125.2 million Omani rials. ($1=0.377 Omani rials)
